chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: Lucky Roberts's call and the 'Junkman Rag'
summary: Retelling how Lucky Roberts and singer Charles Purcell gave him his start at 666 Fifth Avenue, and Roberts's tune played for the president of France.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I nearly starved here in New York. And then finally I got myself together, I got a band, and I used to play all around New York. But first, before that, Lucky Roberts called me ...
He was a club date man.
Yeah, and he said, 'Can you work tonight?' and I said 'Yep' and he said, 'Come up here and I'll brief you on some of the music.' Charlie Purcell was the singer. So --
Who was that again?
Charles Purcell, and we went down to 666 Fifth Avenue, and there was three couples, and we played songs, music, and he sang -- it only lasted a couple hours.
The party was brief, you know, and like I said, it'd be $35, and then -- that's what started me.
That's been the 20's, wasn't it?
Yeah, way back there in the twenties.
And the teens, too.
Wow.
I started rumping them; see, I got myself --
Lucky was a piano player, too -- what did he do?
Lucky was running that place up there.
: What place?
He had his own bar and grill.
: Is that so? Uptown?
A house on 149th Street, on St. Nicholas Avenue.
: On St. Nick?
Yeah.
: What did he call it?
The ... oh, what was it? I don't know, I forget.
: He wrote a couple of very profitable songs, too, didn't he?
Yeah, when I was in the army. 'Junkman's Rag' -- we played that for the President of France, President Pointcaire.
: And that was Lucky Roberts's tune.
That was Lucky Roberts's tune. 'Junkman's Rag.'
: Uh huh. You wouldn't happen to know where we could find some of that music, do you?
Well --
: How'd it go now?
Da, da, da, da ...
: Maybe I'll ask you to play me a couple bars of it later. Okay?
Right, I never played it -- it just came to me.
